what_was_done: The fix raises the last loop 1's used to the stored closure verdict's rounds_used (_closure_rounds_used, passed to _rebuild as stored_used). That count cannot tell an earlier run's passes from this run's own. summary() writes rounds_used = max(passes_used over every run, the stored count), so once the checkpoint stores summary() (survey-2.md 3.5, `verdict`) the closure counts the loop's own passes, and the replay then starts that loop as if they had been used before it. A probe in a scratch copy showed this. Pass 1 has a finding the fixer disputes, pass 2 has the claim not_resolved, and at pass 3 the arbiter rules not_defect. verdict() gives converged/clean with rounds_used 3, and covering() returns it. Store summary() as the closure verdict, as the checkpoint will, and the same records give blocked/cap with rounds_used 6 and code:a blocking, and covering() returns None. A plain two-pass convergence keeps converged but reports rounds_used 4 instead of 2, which breaks D13 ('the full verdict keeps the script's used + pass'). The clone case the finding is about is not settled either: on a clone with stored count N and P > N local passes, the checkpoint stores P, and the replay then uses P where the script was given N. test_replay_uses_the_used_the_script_was_given never stores summary() after the passes, so it cannot see any of this. The regression itself is recorded as S4R-verdicts-C1-1. Still to do: remove the floor so a loop 1's used is again the loop-1 passes of earlier runs (plan rule 9). Add a test that stores summary() into the closure and asserts that verdict() and covering() do not change. Take the clone case to the spec steward: the replay needs the used the run was given, and only a record can hold it (for example the unit's rounds_used, stored on the run when the survey hands it to the script). A closure count written after the run's own passes cannot recover it.
